summary: Controlled replacements favor a Colorado/local-information account over a pure phone-formatting rival. At a fixed pre-contact boundary, Denver (158), Colorado (152), Boulder (130) and Aurora (34) far exceeded matched off-region places (range -14.3 to 1.1) and generic controls (2.2 and 3.0). At a place-token sweep, Colorado places reached 100-116 while off-region places stayed below 7, and numeric off-region contact inputs peaked at only 9.75. The negative tail is weaker and mostly reflects absence of the positive Colorado drive: off-region record cues sat near zero or negative (North Dakota -17.0) while Colorado controls were strongly positive. Blind tests reproduced the semantic contrast (best +354 and -32.5) but did not exceed the saved extremes (+364 and -55.25). One Denver-team graph showed a contrary, context-specific output effect, so the output role is not settled.

p1.name: Local phone-boundary outlier
p1.description: The single top-product graph ends a long workplace-productivity article at a space before a 303 contact number. Its upstream flow is dominated by L38_N489 and L51_N4854, with additional L54_N2872 contribution; this is a contact-boundary outlier rather than a place-name token.

p2.name: Cross-region contact-to-place boundary
p2.description: A New Mexico solar-garden press release lists several office phone numbers and ends before the continuation 'Carbondale, CO'. The graph mixes off-region contact formatting with an imminent Colorado place, making it the strongest boundary case against a simple Colorado-only account.

p3.name: Colorado place and local-listing route
p3.description: Ten natural graphs combine Colorado places, teams, venues, real-estate listings and community features. Shared upstream flow comes from L14_N489, L6_N7831, L38_N489, L49_N12697 and L31_N11703; the route also contains a local-running post without an explicit Colorado name.

n1.name: Off-region contact and record route
n1.description: Utah county and senior-service phone boundaries, an Arizona legal listing, a Montana ecology report and a personal field-work narrative. Flow is led by L37_N171 and L51_N4854 with mixed L52_N15786 and L38_N8626 contributions; the route crosses contact, record and narrative semantics.

n2.name: Public-health and institutional-document route
n2.description: North Dakota public-health and licensing lines, state facts, a nursing-program list and a child-support statute, plus a weak Nebraska innovation feature. L35_N10229 and L37_N10370 carry the most negative upstream weight, with L47_N2209 and L6_N24380 mixed in.

n3.name: Weak sports-opinion and fragment route
n3.description: Two low-amplitude sports-opinion graphs and a three-token 'Owned and operated by AZ Party' fragment. Products are only -1.09 to -3.72, and upstream weights are weak and heterogeneous; this route is retained as an unresolved background factor rather than a semantic class.

clusters.name: Local contact and listing boundaries
clusters.story: Members share an anchor at a phone, address, MLS, registration or place-continuation boundary on local business and listing pages. The top-product productivity page and the New Mexico-to-Colorado press release are boundary cases: both contain contact formatting without a complete Colorado prefix, so the cluster is not purely place-name driven. One product-catalogue graph broadens the membership.

clusters.name: Colorado place, team, and local-culture contexts
clusters.story: Members contain explicit Colorado, Denver or Boulder cues in venue, school, sports, environmental or political contexts, with anchors at spaces, punctuation or function words before a local continuation. The local 5k post lacks an explicit Colorado name and is retained as the main membership exception; lower-amplitude NHL and convention examples show weaker place effects.

clusters.name: Off-region public-service contact lines
clusters.story: These four members place the anchor inside or immediately before non-Colorado public-service telephone numbers: Utah sheriff and senior-center lines and North Dakota health and licensing lines. They share the strongest negative products and negative L35_N10229/L37_N171 upstream flow. The off-region service-contact frame, not an anti-Colorado concept, is the common observation.

clusters.name: Government, legal, and education records
clusters.story: This cluster contains legal, statutory, state-fact and nursing-program documents whose anchors fall on record punctuation, digits or course-list boundaries. Products range from -51.25 to -7.94. Colorado counters are absent; shared negative upstream contributions from L35_N10229 and L37_N10370 link the members despite different document genres.

clusters.name: Science and regional-development reporting
clusters.story: The ecology report and Nebraska regional-development feature share institutional or scientific prose but differ in content and amplitude (-11.81 versus -2.41). No single semantic account joins them; they are kept as an either-pole mixed cluster because a small numerical route crosses unrelated document types.

clusters.name: Near-zero sports commentary
clusters.story: Both sports-opinion members are near-zero (-0.80 and -1.09) and occur at sentence punctuation or a function word in NFL and college-football commentary. They do not support a distinct sports-negative mechanism; the shared observation is weak late-sentence output in sports prose.

clusters.name: Personal narrative and ambiguous fragment
clusters.story: The personal fire-crew narrative reaches -44.75 at ' Spring', whereas the three-token AZ Party fragment is only -3.72. They share no topic or upstream pattern, so this is an unresolved either-pole cluster; retaining both prevents the strong narrative negative from being absorbed into a semantic claim.

spectrum.summary: Fourteen semantic groups describe 434 saved positions. Colorado local information (n=19) and Colorado sports and culture (n=7) are positive throughout, while off-region contacts (33), government and legal records (20), health and social services (23), sports commentary (22) and off-region place description (37) supply most of the negative tail; 212 positions remain mixed or background.

search.summary: At the shared pre-contact boundary, Denver (158), Colorado (152), Boulder (130) and Aurora (34) exceeded Salt Lake City (0.95), Phoenix (1.13), Seattle (-0.91) and Fargo (-14.3); generic controls were 2.16 and 3.05. Numeric off-region contact inputs reached only 9.75 (control median 2.09). At the record boundary, off-region places stayed near zero or negative while Colorado controls were strongly positive.

clusters.summary: The 26 measured route members form seven reader-facing clusters. Positive clusters separate local contact and listing boundaries from Colorado place, team and culture mentions; negative clusters separate public-service contact lines from government, legal and education records. Two small clusters remain mixed or unresolved.

anatomy.summary: At the saved maximum, gate 20.25 and value 18.0 multiply to 364. The selected trace ends a workplace-productivity page at a space before a 303 contact number; zeroing the neuron lowers the local '3' probability from 0.744 to 0.382 and gives KL 0.495 versus at most 0.0015 for same-layer controls.
anatomy.strip_caption: The selected saved trace ends a long workplace-productivity article at a space before a 303 telephone number. Gate and value open together at the anchor, and zeroing the neuron sharply lowers the local '3' probability, consistent with a contact-number boundary response.

ablation.summary: Direct output weights promote Boulder (+0.743), Colorado (+0.729) and Denver (+0.722). Zeroing is context-specific: the median KL is 0.112 across 30 natural cases versus 0.00027 for same-layer random controls; some contact-boundary cases shift strongly, while others are nearly unaffected.

family.summary: Across eleven authored inputs the target is strongly positive for Colorado cues (median 51.9) and near zero for off-region cues (median -0.74). Downstream units at layers 58-63 show both positive and negative Colorado-related responses, so the surrounding circuit is not a single sign.

circuit.summary: Upstream flow is led by L38_N489, L14_N489, L49_N12697, L6_N7831 and L31_N11703. Among thirty downstream readers, positive and negative Colorado-linked responses coexist, so this is not one unidirectional local circuit.

tests.summary: The frozen writer's best positive candidate reached 354 against the 364 corpus maximum, and its strongest negative reached -32.5 against -55.25; neither beat the saved extreme. Both blind sets reproduced Colorado-linked contact and off-region record boundaries, matching the measured semantics but not the full magnitude. Route prediction was disabled.
